items.title: Advancements in Pipeline Corrosion Monitoring for Supercritical CO2 Environments: A Review
items.source: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
items.summary: A review of corrosion evaluation and monitoring techniques for pipelines carrying CO2 in the supercritical state. The authors note that impurities such as water, SO2, O2, H2S and NO2 make supercritical-CO2 corrosion a major challenge for pipeline transport, and that earlier reviews focused on mechanisms and prevention rather than monitoring.
items.why_it_matters: Impurity limits and corrosion monitoring requirements shape CO2 stream specifications, pipeline material choices and operating costs in shared multi-emitter pipeline networks.
items.authors: Prosper Dadzie, Aliyu Adebayo Sulaimon, Shiferaw Regassa Jufar, Yen Adams Sokama‐Neuyam, Joshua Nsiah Turkson, Muhammad Ayoub et al.

items.title: CO2 Transport and Storage Cost Review Webinar
items.summary: Free hybrid IEAGHG webinar on 1 December 2026 (09:00–10:00). Colin Laing and Phoebe Johnston of Xodus Group present findings from a review of CO2 transport and storage costs and later work, covering key cost drivers, the limits of historical cost estimates, and the need for more standardisation and better industry data.
items.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to cost parameters for transport and storage in network-optimisation models; discusses reliability of the cost data such models depend on.

items.title: One year of Longship operations: What's next for CCS in Europe?
items.summary: Workshop organised by Northern Lights with support from Carbon Management Europe, held in Brussels on 2 December 2026 (17:00–19:00) as a side event to the Industrial Carbon Management Summit. It reflects on Northern Lights' first year of operations, with Phase 2 expansion underway, and discusses how to expand CCS in Europe.
items.why_it_matters: First-year operating experience from the Longship ship-based chain is a rare real-world reference for shipping, terminal and storage-capacity assumptions in Nordic network models.

items.title: Industrial Carbon Management Summit 2026
items.summary: Annual Brussels summit of Europe's industrial carbon management community on 3 December 2026 (08:30–18:00), under the theme "Setting the conditions for scale". It covers policies, market frameworks and investment conditions as European CCS projects move toward large-scale deployment.
items.why_it_matters: EU market-framework and investment discussions shape the regulatory and commercial conditions for cross-border CO2 flows from Nordic-Baltic emitters to North Sea storage.

items.title: Central and Southern Europe CCS & CDR Conference: Building on Hungary's strengths to create a regional carbon management hub
items.summary: One-day conference in Budapest on 11 February 2027, organised by Danube Carbon Storage, CSFK and Carbon Management Europe, with an optional site visit to the Danube Removals project on 12 February. Topics include EU policy and funding, subsurface monitoring, the business case for CCS, carbon removals and a roundtable on a Central European hub concept.
items.why_it_matters: Discussion of the regional hub concept for an inland, non-North-Sea region offers a comparison for hub-and-cluster design questions in Nordic-Baltic network planning.

items.title: CNPC Commissions China's Longest CO2 Pipeline
items.summary: CNPC has commissioned the 277.6 km Jilin Petrochemical–Jilin Oilfield CO2 transmission pipeline in Jilin Province, with annual capacity of up to 3.3 million tonnes and a design pressure of 14.5 MPa. It is fed by Jilin Petrochemical's 800,000 t/yr CO2 recovery unit and carries CO2 to the Jilin Oilfield for enhanced oil recovery and geological storage; CNPC plans to offer spare capacity to third-party emitters.
items.why_it_matters: A long-distance, high-pressure trunk line built with spare capacity for third-party emitters is a reference case for pipeline sizing and open-access trunk design in multi-emitter networks.
